subject: Request: adjust reserved tenor and GPU-cost sharing for Novena pilot
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novena.health>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novena.health; aaron.lee@cloudbroker.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Request: adjust reserved tenor and GPU-cost sharing for Novena pilot

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the pilot run last month — performance looked good and the Novena clinical team is eager to expand. Before we sign the reserved capacity term sheet, procurement flagged a material change in GPU market pricing: several cloud GPU vendors pushed a mid-quarter price increase that materially widens the delta between our forecast and your locked SKU pricing.

For a long-term reserve we need a mechanism to protect against sustained GPU-price spikes. Specifically we're asking for either:
- a 24-month tenor with a GPU-cost-sharing corridor (Novena pays a fixed discount up to X% of market deviation, Redwood absorbs beyond that), or
- a shorter 12-month tenor with a mid-term repricing trigger tied to a public GPU index.

Can your team share a version of the term sheet that includes a price corridor or repricing trigger? We can sign quickly if we land on a path that limits our exposure.

Also looping Aaron from our cloud broker — he recommended Redwood and will help with the technical sizing.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Procurement
Novena Health

Attachments: none
From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novena.health>
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com; kimberly.park@redwood.com; david.kim@redwood.com; aaron.lee@cloudbroker.com; procurement@novena.health
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: adjust reserved tenor and GPU-cost sharing for Novena pilot

Elena — really glad Novena is ready to expand, and appreciate the clear ask.

We can propose two workable constructs:
1) 24-month tenor + price-corridor: Redwood historically offers a corridor discount band where small market moves are absorbed by the customer up to a cap (e.g., +/-10% of benchmark), and Redwood covers excess volatility. That reduces bill shock while keeping list pricing predictable.
2) 12-month tenor + index-trigger: a mid-term repricing window tied to a published GPU spot index (we've used the Cloud GPU Index) with a 30-day notice and a one-time repricing adjustment band.

I've pulled in Stephanie (legal) and Kimberly (finance) to validate risk and contract language. David will help size the fleet and confirm burst allowances so we can adjust reserved SKUs without operational disruption.

I'm attaching a draft term sheet with the corridor language (Novena_Redwood_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf). Kimberly — can you run a quick sensitivity for the two constructs and confirm discount/approval thresholds?

Next steps:
- Kimberly: pricing sensitivity (by EOD Wed)
- Stephanie: legal wording for corridor vs index-trigger (by Thu)
- David: updated sizing for 12 vs 24 months (by Thu)
- Elena/Aaron: confirm preferred tenor so we can produce a signature-ready DocuSign.

Thanks — I'll coordinate an internal exec-approval call if Kimberly flags anything above our delegated discount band.

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jul 21, 2026 at 11:02 AM markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena — really glad Novena is ready to expand, and appreciate the clear ask.
> 
> We can propose two workable constructs:

Quick notes on contract risk and practical language:
- Corridor approach: document as a monthly reconciliation where we compute a public GPU index vs. agreed baseline. Pricing adjustments are applied quarterly with caps: customer pays movements within +/-10% of baseline; Redwood absorbs movements beyond +30% (we can negotiate the breakpoints). Include an annual cap on cumulative retroactive adjustments to avoid runaway backcharges.
- Index-trigger approach: requires a clear index source, methodology for lookback window (30/60/90 days), and a one-time mid-term repricing allowance (we should limit to one repricing in 12 months).

For both approaches, include standard protections: maximum annual adjustment cap, notice windows, and mutual audit rights. From a legal standpoint, corridor language must map to billing system reconciliation to avoid disputes.

I've redlined the term sheet (see markup in the attached PDF), and propose the following clause for quick consideration: 
"Price Corridor: For the term of the Agreement, adjustments to per-unit reserved pricing will be reconciled quarterly against the Redwood GPU Index. Novena will be responsible for deviations up to 12% of baseline; deviations beyond 12% and up to 35% will be split 50/50; deviations above 35% will be borne by Redwood up to an annual cap of 15% of total committed spend."

If Mark wants to move fast, we can present both constructs to Novena in one call and recommend the corridor for multi-year stability.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: adjust reserved tenor and GPU-cost sharing for Novena pilot

Markus/Team — I ran the sensitivity using three market scenarios and the attached workbook (GPU-Pricing-Scenario.xlsx). High level:

Scenario A (stable): market stays within +/-8% -> 24-month corridor has negligible impact on unit economics, gives Novena predictable cost and improves Redwood cash visibility.
Scenario B (moderate spike): market +20% sustained for 6 months -> corridor split (our suggested 50/50 in middle band) requires a one-time credit from Redwood ~5% of committed spend under the 24-month option.
Scenario C (severe spike): market +40% sustained -> exposes Redwood to ~12-15% concession for the year under the corridor with our current proposed caps.

Decision boundaries for commercial approval:
- Discounting or cost-sharing that creates >8% estimated revenue impact for Redwood on this deal will need VP-level sign-off.
- Anything >15% impact should escalate to CFO + GTM leadership.

Recommendation: present Novena with the 24-month corridor but tighten breakpoints: customer absorbs up to 10%; split 50/50 for 10-30%; Redwood absorbs above 30% up to annual cap of 12% committed spend. That keeps expected Redwood exposure in the ~5-8% band under moderate scenarios (acceptable for VP approval).

I'll prepare the short exec note if we need sign-off.

Attachment: GPU-Pricing-Scenario.xlsx

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks for the patience while we modeled this. Short summary and ask: 

1) We can do a 24-month reserved tenor with a price corridor. Proposed breakpoints (recommended): Novena pays deviations up to 10%; deviations between 10% and 30% are split 50/50; Redwood absorbs above 30% up to an annual cap equal to 12% of committed spend.
2) Under our finance sensitivity this keeps Redwood's expected exposure within VP-delegated approvals. Anything beyond that would need exec sign-off; we don't expect to hit that in our base case.
3) Attached is the finalized term sheet (redline incorporated) and the pricing scenario workbook. Once Novena confirms the 24-month corridor path we'll generate a signature-ready DocuSign and schedule a 30-minute exec call next week to close commercial approvals.

Proposed immediate next step: Elena — please confirm "accept corridor" or "request index-trigger" by end of day Monday. If you accept corridor, we'll send the DocuSign link and target a signature window this month.
